attribution: MIT News reports research by MIT researchers. This is the originating institution's account, not independent corroboration.

facts.text: MIT researchers developed HardFlow to steer generation toward final outputs that meet hard constraints, without requiring every intermediate sample to meet them.
MIT reports experiments across robotics, control of physical processes and computer vision in which the method satisfied required constraints and found better solutions than existing techniques.
The technique can operate on pretrained generative models at deployment time without retraining.

Forcing intermediate samples to satisfy constraints can prevent a better final solution. HardFlow treats sampling as trajectory optimization, using optimal control to make corrections while enforcing final-output constraints.

MIT says the optimization formulation can include additional quality goals. Its example is a robot path that both avoids collisions and minimizes distance. This example is a capability described with could, not evidence of a deployed system.
